rv.q: "The book is the evening’s weak spot. The dialogue is sometimes so bald it could use an emergency toupet...Bolstered by ingenious, fast-moving, projection-enlivened scenery, expert choreography and sure direction, the cast have a platinum-plated ball...Confronting us with energy and spirit of that irrepressible order, the show moves beyond...
The musical's book is a shaky vehicle largely designed to facilitate the songs.
But 'Motown, the Musical' shines far less brightly, lacking smarts as well as soul.
It is thrilling to see so much exceptional talent on one stage.

While we here in Britain were listening to The Rolling Stones, The Beatles and Cliff Richard and The Shadows, most of America was listening to the extraordinary output and music of Berry Gordy, the founder and owner of the (Tamla) Motown label.
'Motown The Musical' is two and a half hours of musical happiness, and I had an absolute blast.
Squeezing the well-known hits into one show proves hard especially when there is a story to tell and the first half suffers from medley-itis at times.

cn.t: Critics agree the book is weak and simplistic, but the 50+ Motown hits, delivered with energy and pizzazz by a talented cast, make for an exhilarating nostalgia fest that audiences will love despite its lack of depth.
